newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at 5.5/6.0 percent on Tuesday morning, dealers said.
They said the market remained ample following a supply of 789 billion rupiah from the central bank into the market.
One local bank dealer said weekly tax payments due Tuesday were insignificant and this caused short-term rates to fall.
He said longer-term rates were soft but well supported on the downside due to the upcoming new reserve requirement rate of five percent effective from April 16 and the general election on May 29.
One-month money was quoted at 11.375/11.50 percent and three-month at 12.5/13.0 percent, respectively.
One state bank dealer said there was a perception in the market that rupiah supply might continue to be ample until Thursday before it turns tight on Friday.
She said weekly tax payments, month-end and weekend factors would all fall on this Friday.
The central bank did not offer overnight bilateral papers (SBIs) on Tuesday. It kept all bilateral rates stable.
The bank offered seven-day SBIs at seven percent, two-week at nine percent, one- and three-month at 11.0 and 12.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Monday was 6.09 percent, compared with 7.62 percent last Friday.
Bond dealers said prices were stable in slow trading.
The yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was last at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
